info.description: Students develop and apply critical reading skills through the analysis of texts taken from authentic sources (journals, newspapers, magazines and websites) and a variety of academic disciplines. Students are encouraged to develop their comprehension, while at the same time forming a reasoned assessment of the effectiveness and validity of the text.

materials.materialDescription: Mindscapes: Critical Reading Skills and Strategies

clos.loDetails: Analyze the key components of a critical review; differentiate between a critical review and a research essay; structure a critical review

Evaluate whether or not a text is academic; describe the peer-review process works; evaluate why peer-reviewed texts are preferable for academic study; understand the importance of the publication date of a text
Analyze the importance of knowing something about the author of a text and the people quoted by the author; recognize and reason bias
Identify the author’s stance; how the author’s intended audience influences the text; why the author’s purpose is important
Evaluate conclusions drawn from author experience; recognize the steps of the scientific method; evaluate important information as reading reports of empirical research

Identify and evaluate evidence not based on author experience: anecdotes, visual items, statistics and quotations from others; how authors try to persuade readers using no evidence at all; how to evaluate these kinds of evidence

Analyze the importance of considering the text in its broader context; recognize a school of thought and understand the importance of knowing the schools of thought in your area of study; how to approach a text that presents an opinion or theory very different from anything else you have read
Explain why it is important to ask yourself whether the text supports your own experiences; why it can be difficult to do this

Use different reading strategies for different tasks, identify what critical reading is (and what it is not); understand the importance of critical reading skill; make questions and find answers as you read critically; differentiate between critical reading and other reading strategies; Develop and integrate criticality into reading practices.

assessments.questionType: "Assignment 1: LO1-LO3 Option1: Teacher can choose written format (recommended below) or spoken format (specified by class teacher) Based on your reading of the texts in chapters 2 and 3 as well as your own research into these topics, write a short response to the following prompt. You can choose either topic1 or 2 1. Meat is an essential part of a healthy diet. Do you agree or disagree? 2. Sports are about more than just winning and losing; issues related to values and ethics also need consideration. Discuss with reference to one sport or sporting event. Option2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal Assignment 2: LO4-LO5 Option1: Teacher can choose written format (recommended below) or spoken format (specified by class teacher) Based on your reading of the texts in chapter 4 and 5 as well as your own research into these topics, write a short response to the following prompt. You can choose either topic1 or 2 1. How can we solve the energy crisis? Compare and evaluate two or more possible? 2. What qualities, skills and personal characteristics should successful leaders have? Option2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal Assignment 3: LO6-LO7 Option1: Teacher can choose written format (recommended below) or spoken format (specified by class teacher) Based on your reading of the texts in chapters 6 and 7 as well as your own research into these topics, write a short response to the following prompt. You can choose either topic1 or 2 1. Technology is a key component of education in the twenty-first century. Discuss. 2. There is a strong connection between design of the environment and at work or in school. Discuss Option2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal Assignment 4: LO8-LO9 Option1: Teacher can choose written format (recommended below) or spoken format (specified by class teacher) Based on your reading of the texts in chapters 8 and 9 as well as your own research into these topics, write a short response to the following prompt. You can choose either topic1 or 2 1. What is the relationship between the wealth of a country, its economic policies and the happiness of its citizens? 2. What is the value of social networks? Option2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal "
